The edit corrupted the file. Let me inspect and repair it.Done — `IFS=,` is now `IFS=$'\n'`; all other lines are unchanged and `bash -n` passes.

Note: the first edit attempt mangled the file (the tool interpreted the `$'...'` in the replacement), so I rewrote it, verified with `cat -A`, and re-tested. One behavioral caveat: `read -a` stops at the first newline, so a multi-line argument only yields its first field — that's inherent to the requested one-line change, and I left the rest untouched as asked.
